title: Slot-based streaming fallback and adaptive memory sandbox for transient OOMs
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Implement a per-request streaming 'slot' sandbox and soft-admission pipeline to prevent transient OOMs during continuous batching. Provide deterministic fallback to smaller model variants and compact KV snapshots when memory headroom is low, while preserving tail latency and reducing noisy global evictions.
background: We observe transient OOM spikes when large streaming requests with big KV footprints enter continuous batches. Current global eviction strategies cause bursty tail latency and client retries. Previous tickets focused on eviction heuristics and progressive trimming, but we still see high-ish OOM rates under mixed workloads. This initiative aims to isolate inflight streaming requests into memory sandboxes (slots), apply slot-level compaction and admission controls, and implement a model-ladder fallback with deterministic retry semantics.
design_notes: Core ideas: 1) Slot sandbox: allocate a soft memory budget per streaming slot (based on model, sequence length estimate, and KV size). Slots can be compacted (drop cold KV entries, compress activations) without touching other slots. 2) Soft admission queue: requests that would exceed pool headroom are queued briefly (<=30ms) with token-length weighted priority; long requests may be admitted to a lower-priority slot. 3) Slot compaction policies: time-based (inactive for X ms), KV-age-based, and model-aware pruning. 4) Model-ladder fallback: on repeated slot compaction failures, automatically retry request on compatible smaller model (e.g., llama-70B -> llama-13B-quant) with a preserved prompt and deterministic fallback headers for traceability. 5) Metrics: slot_oom_rate, slot_compaction_count, slot_preemptions, soft_admit_delay_ms, fallback_retry_rate.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): implement slot metadata and soft admission gate in serving runtime; add slot-level memory accounting and compaction hooks. Phase 2 (2 sprints): integrate KV compaction routines and lightweight activation compression. Phase 3 (1 sprint): model-ladder fallback engine, deterministic retry headers, and safe rollback. Phase 4: rollout, monitoring, and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: slot_oom_rate reduced by >= 70% on benchmark mixed workload compared to baseline
no increase in p95 latency > 15% for non-fallbacked requests
fallback retry succeeds and returns correct structured status headers for tracing
canary rollout shows stable memory headroom without global evictions for 24h at 10% traffic
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting. Agreed slot abstraction and metrics. Decided to keep compaction non-blocking by default.

2026-03-11: Prototype slot metadata service implemented; added per-slot accounting counters and a soft-admit queue with simple FIFO + length weight. Initial microbench shows 8% overhead on admission path.

2026-03-12: Spike on KV compaction strategies completed. LRU with age threshold + small-value trimming looks promising. Found potential for fragmentation in CUDA allocator during compaction; flagged for allocator team.
2026-03-12: Design review with runtime and infra: agreed to feature-flag full compaction; soft-admit will be default enabled.
blockers: Allocator fragmentation during parallel compaction (tracking in ENG-21333)
Need compatibility matrix for model-ladder fallback (research on semantic parity across variants)
Telemetry tag schema for per-slot tracing not yet finalized (PM input required)
testing_plan: Unit tests for slot accounting and compaction hooks; integration tests with continuous-batching simulator (mixed short/long streaming traffic); chaos tests: force memory pressure to validate compaction and fallback retries; e2e canary validation against production traffic shadow for 48h.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: 1) internal dogfood (0.5% traffic) for 24h; 2) canary 5% traffic for 48h with p99 OOM instrumentation; 3) 25% for 72h; 4) full rollout. Automated rollback if slot_oom_rate increases or p99 latency regresses >25%.
post_deployment_checks: verify no global evictions triggered in pool for 24h
reviewers: Marcus Green - suggested making compaction incremental to avoid allocator churn
Aisha Kapoor - asked to add synthetic load tests for model-ladder to validate quality regression
Jonah Martinez - flagged need for deterministic retry headers for downstream observability
